name: Landing zones between Son and Veghel (centred at Sint-Oedenrode), Noord-Brabant, Netherlands
Logis de la Bocage, Manche
coord_source_note: Stand-in point, not the site: the CMH lists the 1st Infantry Division command post on 4 and 7 August 1944 only as "Logis de la Bocage (vic), Manche" and no gazetteer entry for it was found. The point is Wikipedia (en) Juvigny-le-Tertre, the place of the division command post listed on 3 August ("Juvigny (vic west)"); the earlier point (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, a house in Sartilly) was about 21 km west of Brécey and out of the division's sequence. Site search of 26 October 2026 (open item 6; point and precision unchanged): the name "Logis de la Bocage" was searched in the IGN geocoder (data.geopf.fr, place-name layer: no entry of that name; three hamlets named "le Logis" in Mortain-Bocage at about 48.608 N 0.910 W, 48.592 N 0.997 W and 48.582 N 0.956 W, and the Chateau du Logis at 48.591 N 0.997 W, none tied to the division by any source), OpenStreetMap Nominatim (only Le Vieux Logis, Sartilly, the earlier rejected point), the CMH 1st Infantry Division page (the same two entries, 4 and 7 August, "vic", Manche, no map reference) and the 90th Division after-action report of August 1944 (which has the 1st Division "moving east along the See River on Mortain"); the 1st Division after-action reports and G-3 journal (Eisenhower Library, accession 64-3) are not online. Breakout and Pursuit ch. 23 (pp. 443-445) has the division enter Mortain on the afternoon of 3 August and on 6 August displace south across the Selune to Gorron and Ambrieres-le-Grand. No source locates the site, so the stand-in is kept.
